html/entities#

HTML escaping and unescaping of text.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

EscapedHtml("<Ada & Bob>").string();                   // "&lt;Ada &amp; Bob&gt;"
EscapedHtml(origin: title, quotes: true).string();     // for attribute values
UnescapedHtml("caf&eacute; &lt;3").string();           // "café <3"

Description#

HTML escaping and unescaping of text.

Escaping is not sanitizing: it makes text safe as text or as a quoted attribute value, nothing more. Unescaping knows all 2231 named references of the HTML standard.

Public API#

object EscapedHtml#

object EscapedHtml

Text with &, < and > escaped, and quotes too when asked.

EscapedHtml.EscapedHtml#

EscapedHtml(origin is string)

Escapes origin for text.

EscapedHtml.EscapedHtml#

Escapes origin; quotes also escapes " and ' for attribute values.

EscapedHtml.string#

string() is string

The escaped text; existing references are escaped again.

object UnescapedHtml#

object UnescapedHtml

Character-reference-decoded text, using HTML text-context recovery rules. Construction retains source only. string() decodes once, preserving literal markup and all non-reference scalars (including NUL and CRLF). Unknown names and digitless numeric references stay literal; invalid numeric scalars become U+FFFD and HTML C1 replacements apply. This is not attribute-context decoding, document parsing, sanitization or recursive decoding of the resulting text. The hidden tokenizer uses the pinned 2231-spelling table in Okkama. Example: UnescapedHtml("<b>&lt;</b>").string() == "<b><</b>". Each observation uses O(n) temporary memory; no native registry handle, external resources or I/O. Repeated observations agree.

UnescapedHtml.UnescapedHtml#

UnescapedHtml(origin is string)

The text.

UnescapedHtml.string#

string() is string

The decoded text; unknown names stay as written.
